Glaziers and Architectural Metal

IUPAT DC 16 — International Union of Painters and Allied Trades, District Council 16 glaziers apprenticeship

IUPAT District Council 16 glaziers apprenticeship and training in architectural glass and metal, the IUPAT Finishing Trades Institute glazier curriculum, ANSI/ASSP Z97.1 safety glazing materials, and OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subparts L and M for scaffolds and fall protection

A glass and metal crew across a whole building: a unit walked off the floor, a storefront glazed with cups, a yard that hands lites from a trailer to a rack, a swing stage over the plaza, a skylight opened only under a screen, a shattered lite cleared and covered, a shop that bends and squares the panel before it ever ships, and the field measure an order is actually cut against.

20 / 20levels at 75+ lessons
1741lessons across the track
120tasks: a station under a condition
0more stations needed to fill it

Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Level 1 is open; each level opens when the one below is passed — every task in one run of it a mastery run. A task opens its station with its condition; the number after each task is its steps.

Construction & Structural Trades

Curtain Wall Unit Setting From The Floor

15 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min

A pre-glazed unit is walked off the floor stack on a davit and anchored into a bay that is a straight fall to the street for as long as it stays open, so the barrier, the harness and the wind reading all come before the unit does.

  • union — IUPAT District Council 16 — glaziers apprenticeship and training, architectural glass and metal
  • union — IUPAT Finishing Trades Institute — industrial painter, glazier and drywall finisher apprenticeship, including lead and containment training
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926.501 — Duty to have fall protection
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926.502 — Fall protection systems criteria and practices

Glass Handling Cart And Crane Vacuum Lifter

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 4.8 min

Every lite in the yard changes hands twice before it is cut, and both the crane's vacuum beam and the hand cups fail the same way — a reading trusted without being read — so both get proven empty before either carries a real lite.

Swing Stage Glazing And Sealant

15 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.1 min

Two wire ropes hold a swing stage over the plaza, and the rope grab on its own separate lifeline is the only thing that holds the person if either one lets go, so it stays clipped and sliding the whole time anyone is on the platform.

Skylight Glass Replacement And Fall Protection

15 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 4.9 min

A skylight curb with no glass and no screen in it looks like the rest of the roof from three steps away and is a straight fall through, so the screen and the warning line go up before the old unit ever comes loose and stay up until the new one is sealed.

Aluminium Panel Fabrication And Brake

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 4.6 min

A press brake closes on tonnes at a pace slow enough to look harmless and fast enough to give a hand no time back, so the two-hand control is proven empty and held through every cycle rather than trusted to a single foot pedal.

Shop Drawing Takeoff And Field Measure

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 4.5 min

A lite ordered to the drawing instead of the actual opening arrives and does not fit, so the field measurement — width, height and both diagonals, taken from a scaffold that is locked before it is climbed — is what the shop cuts glass against.

What it proves

Competency: Set, seal and clear architectural glass under fall protection, from the floor, the yard or a swing stage

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 4 of its 8 stations, against union IUPAT District Council 16 — glaziers apprenticeship and training, architectural glass and metal; ANSI/ASSP Z97.1 Safety glazing materials used in buildings; OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart L Scaffolds; OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart M Fall protection; ANSI/ASSP Z359 Fall Protection Code.

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: IUPAT District Council 16 glaziers apprenticeship and training in architectural glass and metal, the IUPAT Finishing Trades Institute glazier curriculum, ANSI/ASSP Z97.1 safety glazing materials, and OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subparts L and M for scaffolds and fall protection. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
